sources.entry: Loading - Simple network activity monitor for macOS.

summary.one_liner: Loading is a small macOS menu bar app that shows a spinning progress wheel while the network is in use and lists which apps are using it.
summary.what_it_does: Shows a spinning progress wheel in the Mac menu bar whenever the network is being used, similar to the iOS network activity indicator. Clicking the icon shows the apps currently using the network. Holding down the Option key switches the menu to show individual processes. The README says most of the functionality was reverse-engineered from the private NetworkStatistics framework in /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks. It also describes several workarounds for NSMenu and NSStatusItem bugs in macOS, which are mostly developer notes. The README lists the app in more than 30 languages.
use_cases: see which Mac apps are using the network
monitor network activity from the menu bar
find which process is using bandwidth
check whether a background app is sending or receiving data
stack: Objective-C/Cocoa (implied by NSMenu and NSStatusItem references)
notable: Spinning menu bar icon appears only while the network is active
Option-key hold reveals per-process network usage
Reverse-engineered from the private NetworkStatistics framework
Detailed write-up of macOS NSMenu and NSStatusItem bugs and workarounds
caveats: Relies on a private macOS framework and selectors, which may break in future macOS releases
Support for OS X versions older than 10.7 is untested
The README gives no install or download instructions; the Website and Download links are empty in the text
